mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a housing starts contraction (HOUST) signals weakening aggregate demand, which depresses corporate earnings and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND HOUST monthly change < -10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate increase above 5.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate hiring, which in turn leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 5.5% AND UNRATE monthly change > +0.3pp for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.3%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months signals a contraction in economic output, which reduces corporate revenues and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the federal funds rate below 1% combined with a concurrent collapse in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 1% signals a deep recessionary environment, which drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real personal savings (proxied by RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average, coincident with a decline in personal consumption expenditures growth (GDPC1), signals a shift from spending to saving, which reduces demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-month RSAFS MA AND GDPC1 YoY growth < 0%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6% without a corresponding decline in payrolls (PAYEMS) signals persistent labor market weakness, which depresses consumer demand and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 6% AND PAYEMS monthly change < -50,000 for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.7%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A consistent monthly increase in housing starts (HOUST) above 5% for three consecutive months signals a robust residential construction cycle, which boosts demand for materials and labor, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST monthly change > +5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
